title: [negative result] HyDE cost 2 model calls per query and did not clear the band
body:
> **Casebook thread.** A reconstructed conversation, written for teaching. The people in it
> are illustrative; **every number is real** and reproducible from the notebook cited below.
> Replies are welcome — if you hit this yourself, add your numbers.

### What I tried

HyDE — generate a hypothetical answer to the query, embed *that* instead of the query, retrieve
against it. [#9](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/issues/9) proposes it; I wanted to know
whether to close that issue.

### The result

```text
                     evidence_recall   full_chain   latency p95   calls/query
baseline (hybrid)          0.807          0.686         310 ms         0
+ HyDE                     0.821          0.691       1,240 ms         1
delta                     +0.0140       +0.0050
95% CI                [-0.0071, +0.0356]  [-0.031, +0.041]
verdict            inside the band   inside the band
```

**Four times the latency and a model call per query, for a delta whose interval crosses zero.**

### Why I think it did not help here

**1 · The vocabulary gap it fixes is small on this corpus.** HyDE helps when the query and the
documents use different language — a short colloquial question against formal prose. Our eval
questions are generated from the same fact graph as the documents, so they already share
vocabulary. **The corpus construction removes the problem HyDE solves.**

**2 · The lexical leg was already covering it.** Slicing by class, the only questions where HyDE
moved anything were `inference` ones, where the +0.031 was real in isolation but is one class out
of four and does not survive the multiple-comparison argument.

### What I would tell a client

HyDE is a real technique with a real mechanism, and the mechanism is **vocabulary mismatch
between queries and documents.** Measure that gap before paying for it: sample 30 queries, look
at whether the terms people use appear in the documents at all. If they do, HyDE has nothing to
close.

### What this cost me

Two hours, and I would rather have this result than the version where I ship it because the
point estimate was positive.

comments.body:
> **Marcus** · cohort peer

Pushing back on closing #9 off this. Your generator for the hypothetical document is the
extractive one, isn't it? That cannot write a plausible hypothetical answer — it can only copy
sentences that are already in the corpus.

If so, you have not tested HyDE. You have tested "retrieve with a slightly different query made
of corpus text", which is nearly a no-op.

replies.body:
> **Priya** · cohort peer

Checking the write-up — it says one model call per query, so it is not the extractive path.
Marcus's objection would be decisive if it were, though, and it is the first thing I would have
asked too.

> **Marcus** · cohort peer

Fair, I misread the calls/query column. Withdrawn — though it is worth the write-up saying
*which* generator explicitly, because that is the first thing anyone will check.

comments.body:
> **Dana** · reviewer · owns the eval harness

Endorsing the finding and the framing, with one addition that makes it more reusable.

**The transferable form is a precondition, not a verdict.** "HyDE did not help" is corpus-specific
and near-useless to the next reader. "**HyDE closes a vocabulary gap between queries and
documents; measure the gap before paying for it**" transfers to every corpus.

The diagnostic in the last section is the valuable part and should be promoted above the numbers:
sample 30 queries, check whether their terms appear in the documents at all. That is ten minutes
and it tells you whether the technique has anything to do.

**Not closing [#9](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/issues/9).** It stays open with this
thread linked and the precondition written into it, because on a corpus with a real vocabulary
gap the answer would very likely be different — and that is what the issue is now for.
